mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the drop in PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansionary periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the drop in INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent supply chain issues.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, the tight monetary policy combined with a strong labor market signals a potential economic overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent economic overheating indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% YoY and consumer spending (RSAFS) is declining, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of low GDPC1 growth and declining RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent demand weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% signals a weak labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during a recessionary regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE > 8% does not correlate with subsequent recessionary indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 50 basis points in a month signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the drop in FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent accommodative policy actions.
